title: Motion Verbs 5: Prefix при- (arrive)
description: The prefix при- attaches to идти / ехать and turns the verb perfective. The new meaning is arrival: the moment the subject reaches the destination. Past forms only at this stage.
descriptionRussian: Приставка при- присоединяется к «идти» и «ехать» и делает глагол совершенного вида. Новое значение — прибытие: момент достижения цели.
intro: The second prefix marks arriving. The contrast in the past is now four ways: in progress, round trip, setting off, and getting there. All four translate into English as 'went', which is why this is the part of Russian that feels least learnable at first and most obvious once it clicks.
rules: Прийти = perfective of идти; приехать = perfective of ехать. Both mark the moment of ARRIVAL at the destination.
Past forms are the focus today. Foot: пришёл / пришла / пришло / пришли (irregular). Transport: приехал / приехала / приехало / приехали (regular).
Four-way past contrast on foot now: шёл (in progress) vs ходил (round-trip) vs пошёл (onset) vs пришёл (arrival). Same shape for transport: ехал, ездил, поехал, приехал.

Cues that pull the arrival reading: a time of arrival, a sequence where 'arrived' is one event in a list, an 'из + gen' source phrase, a 'когда X пришёл / приехал' clause that captures the step-in moment.
The в / на + acc destination rule from Lesson 3 still applies. The 'из + gen' source phrase ('из школы,' 'из Москвы') is the new piece introduced today.
examples: Антон пришёл домой в шесть часов и сразу лёг спать. (Anton arrived home at six and went straight to bed.) Time of arrival + sequence.
Соня приехала из Петербурга вчера вечером. (Sonya arrived from Petersburg yesterday evening.) 'Из + gen' source phrase.
Когда Лена пришла на встречу, все уже ждали. (When Lena arrived at the meeting, everyone was already waiting.) 'Когда' clause captures the step-in moment.
Гости наконец пришли. (The guests have finally arrived.) The 'наконец' adverb confirms arrival.
Маша пришла на работу вовремя. (Masha got to work on time.) Time-of-arrival reading on an idiomatic 'на' destination.
Иван приехал в Москву на поезде. (Ivan arrived in Moscow by train.) Arrival by transport, with the means phrase.

tables.title: Past tense: four readings of motion

items.prompt: Маша утром _____ на работу на машине.
items.promptEnglish: In the morning Masha set off for work by car.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 4: 'утром' anchors a moment of departure. Fem onset by transport?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 4: 'утром' marks the moment Masha set off; the onset reading carries the perfective поехала (по- prefix, fem). Today's lesson introduces the mirror prefix при- for the moment of arrival, but the warm-up keeps yesterday's по- in working memory.

items.prompt: Антон _____ домой и сразу лёг спать.
items.promptEnglish: Anton came home and immediately went to bed.
items.hint: The bed sequence requires a completed arrival, not motion in progress. Which prefix fits?
items.explanation: 'Сразу лёг спать' is the next event after Anton walks through the door: he arrives, then sleeps. Arrival on foot → пришёл (при- prefix, masc). Шёл would describe motion in progress, awkwardly paired with 'сразу лёг'; пошёл would mark the moment of setting off, the wrong end of the trip; ходил would describe a completed round-trip with no clear arrival moment.

items.prompt: Соня _____ в офис в девять часов.
items.promptEnglish: Sonya arrived at the office at nine.
items.hint: 'В девять часов' names the time of arrival, not the time of departure. Which form fits?
items.explanation: 'В девять часов' on the office side of the trip = the time Sonya stepped through the door. Arrival on foot, fem → пришла. Пошла would mark the moment she left home, which the 'в девять часов в офис' framing rules out (her departure would be earlier). The contrast 'пошла vs пришла' is the cleanest way to feel the prefix difference.

items.promptEnglish: The guests have already arrived at the house.
items.hint: 'Уже' confirms a completed arrival: they are now inside. Plural arrival on foot?
items.explanation: 'Уже' is the canonical completion marker: the action is done. Plural arrival on foot → пришли. Шли would describe them in motion at some past moment; пошли would mark the moment they left for the house, not their being there now; ходили would describe a completed round-trip, contradicting the present-relevance reading 'they are here.'

items.prompt: Иван _____ из Москвы вчера и привёз подарки.
items.promptEnglish: Ivan arrived from Moscow yesterday and brought gifts.
items.hint: 'Из Москвы' marks the source. Which transport form fits the arrival-back reading?
items.explanation: The 'из + gen' phrase names where Ivan came FROM, which only the arrival reading hosts: he is now back, with gifts. Arrival by transport, masc → приехал. Поехал would mean 'set off from Moscow,' which is grammatical but does not match 'привёз подарки' (he could not bring gifts to the speaker if he were just leaving Moscow). Ехал would describe the moment he was on the train; ездил a completed round-trip without a clear arrival moment.

items.prompt: Когда Лена _____ в библиотеку, в зале было много людей.
items.promptEnglish: When Lena arrived at the library, there were many people in the hall.
items.hint: The 'когда' clause captures the step-in moment, not the time on the road. Which form?
items.explanation: The 'когда X пришла, Y' frame anchors the arrival: the speaker is reporting what Lena saw at the moment she walked in. Arrival on foot, fem → пришла. Шла would describe motion in progress, pairing the perception clause with mid-walk noticing, which is awkward. Пошла would mark her departure from elsewhere, on the wrong side of the trip.

items.promptEnglish: Anton arrived at work at nine.
items.hint: Arrival on foot, masculine: which prefix?
items.explanation: Arrival takes при-: пришёл на работу. Пошёл marks setting off (the other end of the trip); шёл is mid-walk; ходил a completed round trip.

items.promptEnglish: Sonya came back from school late in the evening.
items.hint: Coming back = arriving here, from a source.
items.explanation: 'Came back' is the arrival reading: пришла из школы. Пошла would mark departure; ушла would mean she left and is gone; the из + genitive phrase names the source.

items.promptEnglish: The guests arrived from Moscow yesterday.
items.explanation: Arrival by transport takes приехали. Поехали marks departure; ездили a completed round trip (they would be gone and back, not here); ехали is mid-ride.

blanks: Дети _____ в школу в восемь утра. (The kids arrived at school at eight in the morning.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: 'В восемь утра' on the school side of the trip names the time of arrival. Plural arrival on foot → пришли (при- prefix, plural past). Шли would describe motion in progress; пошли the moment of departure; ходили a completed round-trip. The 'в школу в восемь утра' framing pinpoints the moment they walked through the school door.

errorCorrection.sentence: Лена поехала домой в восемь вечера и сразу поужинала.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena arrived home at eight in the evening and immediately had dinner.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'И сразу поужинала' is the event right after Lena gets through the door: she arrives, then eats. Arrival by transport, fem → приехала (при- prefix). Поехала marks the moment of setting off, the wrong end of the trip.

errorCorrection.sentence: Гости поехали из деревни и привезли свежие овощи.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The guests arrived from the village and brought fresh vegetables.
errorCorrection.explanation: The 'из деревни' source plus 'привезли свежие овощи' (brought vegetables here) means the guests have arrived at the speaker's location: приехали (при- prefix). Поехали would mean they set off from the village, but then they could not yet have brought anything to the speaker. Ехали describes motion in progress; ездили a completed round-trip. The 'из + gen' source with an arrival verb names where they came from.

errorCorrection.sentence: Когда мы ехали в офис, все уже сидели за столами.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: When we arrived at the office, everyone was already sitting at their desks.
errorCorrection.explanation: The 'когда X приехал, Y' frame captures the moment of stepping in and seeing the scene: arrival by transport, plural → приехали (при- prefix). Ехали would place the perception mid-ride, but you cannot see colleagues at their desks from the road.

errorCorrection.sentence: Лена приехала в Петербурга в субботу.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena arrived from Petersburg on Saturday.
errorCorrection.explanation: The English 'from Petersburg' names the source, which takes из + genitive: из Петербурга (Петербург → Петербурга, gen sg). The error pairs the preposition в with a genitive form, which never matches: в takes the accusative and names the destination (куда?), while из takes the genitive and names the source (откуда?). 'В Петербург' (accusative) would mean 'to Petersburg,' the wrong direction for an arrival back here.

minimalPairs.context: Антон _____ домой в шесть часов и поужинал.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton arrived home at six and had dinner.
minimalPairs.explanation: The dinner sequence requires a completed arrival: he gets home, then eats. 'В шесть часов' anchors the time of arrival, and 'поужинал' is the next event. Шёл would describe motion in progress, which cannot be paired cleanly with 'поужинал.'

minimalPairs.context: Иван уже _____ из Москвы и устал с дороги.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Ivan has already arrived from Moscow and is tired from the trip.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Уже...Устал с дороги' shows Ivan is now back: he has completed the trip. Arrival reading → приехал. Поехал would mean 'set off from Moscow,' which contradicts the present-tense 'устал' (he could not be back-and-tired if he were just leaving). The 'из Москвы' source phrase confirms direction: away from Moscow, toward the speaker.

minimalPairs.context: Когда Лена _____ в офис, начальник уже сидел за столом.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: When Lena arrived at the office, the boss was already sitting at the desk.
minimalPairs.explanation: The 'когда X пришла, Y' frame catches the moment Lena steps in and sees the scene: arrival on foot, fem → пришла. Пошла marks the moment she set off from elsewhere, the wrong end of the trip: she could not see the boss at his desk while still leaving home.

reviewVocab.definition: Perfective verbs formed with при- + идти / ехать. They mark the moment of arrival at the destination. Past forms пришёл / приехал are the workhorses at this stage.
reviewVocab.example: Антон пришёл домой в шесть часов.

reviewVocab.definition: The 'arrival' prefix in the motion-verb system. Attached to идти / ехать it produces perfective verbs of arrival. It mirrors по- (which marked the onset of motion in Lesson 4): по- = leave for, при- = arrive at.
The genitive-governing preposition that names the source of motion. Pairs with arrival verbs to express where the subject is coming from. The mirror of в + acc destination phrases.
reviewVocab.example: Иван приехал из Москвы вчера вечером.
